correctness.rationale: Independently checked every 6- and 7-subset of the 27 words. Each descendant is represented by the three coordinate symbol sets; equality of these nonempty Cartesian products is exactly equality of the three projections. The check compares the signatures of all nonempty coalitions of size at most 3. There were 135 valid 6-subsets and no valid 7-subsets, which excludes all larger codes by heredity. Direct application of the 1296 distinct isometries to the stated representatives partitions the census into orbits of 27 and 108. Orbit–stabilizer gives 48 and 12, and direct coordinate and pair-projection counting gives exactly the stated profiles. The independently recovered census hash matches the frozen one.
residual_risks: Finite executable enumeration, not a formal proof-assistant certificate or a theorem at other parameters.

evidence: Cheng et al. give the binary maximum 3 and the general q² bound for q>2; their sharper floor(3q²/4) bound is stated for q≥4, with exact q=4 value 12. Zhang et al.'s corresponding numerical theorem is also stated for q≥4.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The binary and q≥4 results do not settle the ternary problem. At q=3 the cited general q² bound is 9, not the claimed exact value.

evidence: The exact same two representatives are listed, with the same coordinate multiplicities. Counting each projection of the first gives one repeated ordered pair and four singletons; each projection of the second gives six distinct pairs.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Independent relabelings preserve the sorted multiplicities of a projection, and coordinate permutations only reorder the projections. The indexed orbit classification therefore implies all projection-profile statements for all maxima. No independent mathematical remainder of the frozen claim survives.
